heartbeat_means: Refreshed when the run writes a line to stdout, at most once per 30 s, or at once when the line changes the stage, and the line it came from is the `stage` in status.json. RayWorkPool prints a progress line only after ray.wait has returned completed work, never sooner than 60 s after its last one, and otherwise only once 300 s have passed or more than 500 queue events have completed since it (RayPoolKit's defaults, which main.py does not override), so a fresh heartbeat from it means work completed within about five minutes. Several of main.py's queues are silent (title=None). Ray also forwards the workers' own output to the driver's stdout, so a worker's line beats too, without moving the stage. It does NOT mean any Ray task or actor is progressing, and the converse does not hold: a stage that prints nothing for longer than the staleness window (900 s, `list --stale-after`), such as a queue whose items each take longer than that, is reported stale while it works, and the gradient branch's solves have run for hours each. Stale means go and look.
